They were the ones who had not stayed until the end I felt sorry. Those who have a bus to catch or a car to move or start early the next day. Imagine going out early. Imagine missing that .

And now everything you have left is an adhesive story about going to the last and most dramatic mecrseyside derby in Goodison Park just to leave before the atomic bomb landed. They are the ghosts of Goodison, the Internet memes that live and breathe.
Not for them adrenaline, shock and amazement pumpled directly to their veins, the dizziness, the heart hitting as a drum. Not for them pure joy. Not for them, the feeling that good things really still happen, even in these more difficult times.
Not for them the reminder that live sport has not yet changed. It is not for them the knowledge that whatever we do and, nevertheless, we seek to put it and disinfect it, what happens there, in the grass where we all really want to be, it still matters more than we can explain.
No, none of that is for them. Maybe they seek to change their history. They may say they were there because during the previous 90 minutes they had been. But deep down, they will know.

In the background they will know that their experience lacked the part that matters, the part that would have kept them awake at night, looking at the roof thanking their mother or dad or aunt or uncle or brother or sister or who is the one who first pushed them time the address of your football team.
And this is not to make fun of those who did not see him, who did not witness that Tarkowski did what few manage to do. No, it is to celebrate those who were there and that they gave testimony of another moment to remind us that football still lives in the deep of us in such a way that it is impossible to delegate.
We all know the list of things that have done us in the name of progress. And when we say progress, to a large extent we mean money.
Starting times, ticket prices, VAR delays, FA cup repetitions, Wembley semifinals. But we also know that in the background where it matters, they cannot touch us. They just can’t take this away.
Football is still visceral and real and representative of life in all its glories and failures and sometimes there is absolutely no substitute for being there to see it.

Ange Postecoglou said the scrutiny about his position in Tottenham is “only things driven by the agenda”
Posttecoglou crystal message
Ange Postecoglou was calm when he delivered his evaluation of Tottenham’s last setback, but his message was clear.
“This is just things driven by the agenda,” said Postecoglou. ‘If it’s to get rid of me, then well with you. If you want to get rid of me, well.
So let’s be clear. Nobody in the main media wants to see postecoglou fired in Tottenham. No one treats it differently because it is Australian, as previously suggested in the season. There is no agenda.
It is being examined by its results, just like everyone else. When suggesting that it is something different, it seems weak when in reality it is not. Managers who see ghosts in the shadows do not tend to last a long time, so it is a look that postecoglou would do well to shake.
He is right when he says that some people do not understand the impact of injuries and exhaustion on their team’s results. And what is worth, I think Tottenham should hold on to him. Let’s see how your team looks when your big players return.
But managers who speak in terms of conspiracy theories often end with one foot outside the door. Posttecoglou must leave that to the crazy people of social networks and continue with his work while he can still.

My colleague Simon Jordan believes that John Eustace will get what comes to him in the future after making it clear that he wants to leave Blackburn for Derby County.
But the fact is that it already has that blow to the solar plexus. Football has already done the best.
Eustace had the sixth city of Birmingham in the championship in October 2023 when he was fired to leave space for Wayne Rooney. Then he knows how football works.
And this is its bump. Why do we expect our managers to follow a code of trusted and loyalty unwritten when the world they live and work on exchanges on convenience and short term? It makes no sense.
It is football that makes people like Eustace behave as they do. Sometimes we get what we deserve.
